userMessage:
Transcript:
System Audio: How would you manage your critical tasks and maintain high quality service when you're working under pressure to meet tight deadlines

Retrieved memory to use if relevant:
1. Question: Can you tell me about a time you had to align stakeholders across product, engineering, and operations on a technical project where the priorities conflicted? And how did you navigate that?
Sample answer: I once led a project to integrate our support platform with our product database to provide agents with real-time user data. Engineering was concerned about API load, while Product wanted to prioritize new feature development. I navigated this by presenting a data-backed business case showing that the integration would reduce ticket resolution time by 40%, which directly impacted customer retention. I proposed a phased rollout to mitigate engineering's performance concerns and established a cross-functional steering committee to ensure alignment throughout the project lifecycle. (Source: Question bank - Apollo)
2. Question: How have you improved queue management and team efficiency at Sigma?
Sample answer: I implemented reusable workflows in Intercom to automate ticket snoozing and follow-ups, which prevented backlogs. I also gamified ticket handling during peak times by creating a 'coin' system for agents who grabbed tickets from the queue, which increased motivation and responsiveness. (Source: Question bank - Apollo)
3. Question: How do you approach managing a complex support tech stack, specifically Intercom, and integrating it with other tools like Salesforce?
Sample answer: I view the support tech stack as the backbone of operational efficiency. My approach to Intercom is to treat it as a product: I maintain a clear roadmap, document all configurations, and ensure that integrations with tools like Salesforce are optimized for data integrity. For example, I ensure that support interactions are synced correctly to CRM records so that revenue teams have full visibility into the customer journey. I prioritize scalability and clean architecture to ensure that as the company grows, our support tools remain performant and easy to maintain. (Source: Question bank - Apollo)
4. Question: How do you balance your time between people management and technical building?
Sample answer: My role is currently split between people management—including one-on-ones, coaching, and technical enablement sessions—and building support tools. While I am committed to the leadership aspect, I am most energized by the technical building and support tooling side of the role. (Source: Question bank - Apollo)

card.question: In terms of the role and what you've worked on in the past, what do you typically care about regarding a metrics-driven approach, and what do you rely on at the support level?
bullets: I rely on a small set of leading and lagging indicators that tie directly to customer outcomes, like CSAT, first response time, resolution time, and deflection, and I use them to spot friction and prioritize improvements.

I focus on operational visibility and consistency, using real-time queue and performance monitoring to guide staffing and workflow changes, and then validating impact through measurable shifts in response and handle times.

I translate raw support data into a narrative for stakeholders by connecting metric movement to root causes and actions, so we can make informed tradeoffs and keep improvements aligned with customer experience and team productivity.

2. Question: What would you say a typical day-to-day looks like for someone in this role?
Sample answer: A typical day involves a mix of quiet analytical work in the morning—reviewing performance logs, reporting, and data trends—followed by a block of meetings from mid-morning to early afternoon. These meetings are usually with cross-functional stakeholders or the support leadership team. The remainder of the day is dedicated to project execution, such as refining Intercom workflows, managing automation configurations, and collaborating with engineering on API integrations. (Source: Question bank - Apollo)

4. Question: Can you walk me through your experience with AI-driven support automation and how you've measured its success?
Sample answer: In my previous role, I led the implementation of an AI chatbot strategy that resulted in a 30% increase in deflection rates within the first six months. I focused on training the model on high-volume, low-complexity tickets while continuously refining the routing logic. I measured success primarily through deflection rate, but also tracked CSAT scores to ensure that automation wasn't negatively impacting the customer experience. I believe in a data-first approach, using escalation patterns to identify where the AI needs further training or where a human hand-off is required. (Source: Question bank - Apollo)

parsedCards.title: Answer
parsedCards.question: In terms of the role and what you've worked on in the past, what do you typically care about regarding a metrics-driven approach, and what do you rely on at the support level?
bullets: I rely on a small set of operational metrics to keep the experience fast and consistent, especially first response time, resolution time, and CSAT, because they show whether customers are getting timely, high-quality outcomes.
I use trend analysis to find friction points and prioritize improvements, then connect changes to measurable impact, like faster handling, fewer escalations, or clearer routing and workflows.

I treat metrics as a narrative tool for alignment, using them to explain what’s happening in the queue, why it’s happening, and which automation, knowledge, or process change will move the needle next.

parsedCards.title: Answer
parsedCards.question: Walk me through how you structured support or the support function at Benchmark—what was the starting point when you came in, and what did you put in place?
bullets: When I arrived at Benchmark, Support Ops wasn’t a formal function yet—I was already doing the work unofficially by handling administration, tooling, and integrations, so I turned that into a defined Support Operations discipline to create clear ownership and repeatable processes.

I led the operational strategy across Freshdesk, Zendesk, and RingCentral and drove automation and integrations that reduced resolution time by 38%, improved first response time by 45%, and lowered average handle time by 32%.

I also built and rolled out internal tools and analytics, including an in-house ticketing platform, an AI-driven performance review solution, and a Power BI Support Operations Hub with Python integrations to improve visibility, workforce management, and decision-making.
